purpose: Per-game evidence table for the additive village-wide mask distribution identity safeguard. Every offset here must already be used by shipped patch code or documented RE for that exact build. Fields without proven evidence are ABSENT, never guessed, and an adapter whose required protections are unproven stays disabled so the existing native planner remains the path taken.

rules.evidence_required: Each field cites the file and definition that establishes it for that exact build. A field with no such citation is omitted from the adapter rather than estimated from a sibling game.
rules.fallback: enabled=false means the safeguard does not run for that game and the existing native planner is used unchanged.
rules.collision_policy: fail_closed: if two candidates share every captured field AND the stable record index cannot separate them, the whole distribution is abandoned with a diagnostic and nothing is written.
rules.evidence_audit: The parentage finding and the VV2/VV4 name offsets were confirmed by an independent RE audit of the four exact builds. Fields that audit could not establish remain absent here.

unproven_fields_global.parentage: Requested for VV2-VV5, defined as the NAME, HEAD and BODY of the villager's mother and father, expected to be stored inline in each villager's own record. An independent RE audit of all four exact builds found NO such fields. Per build, the inheritance path that writes a child's own head/body was identified -- VV2 sub_44C600 -> record+0x548/+0x54C; VV3 sub_456120 -> record+0xDF0/+0xDF4; VV4 sub_45EF10 -> record+0x1BB8/+0x1BBC; VV5 constructor/inheritance/pregnancy/delivery/clone/save-load -> record+0x1BB8/+0x1BBC -- but no instruction was found that stores a mother_name, father_name, mother_head, father_head, mother_body or father_body into the child record. Inheritance computes the child's OWN head; it does not retain the parents' values. Parentage is therefore captured by NO adapter and must not be added without new per-build instruction-level evidence.
unproven_fields_global.elderly_state: No build defines a separately proven elderly flag. Elderly/old rendering is DERIVED from age thresholds -- VV4 and VV5 select the old frame by age. The adapters therefore capture the proven AGE value as `age` and never relabel it as an elderly flag; treat elderly as derived from age unless new instruction evidence appears.

active.evidence: vv1_origins_icons.c VV_OCCUPIED_OFFSET (record[+0x28]==1 when the slot is a live villager)

name.evidence: record+0x370, a 28-byte string buffer (0x370..0x38B). Start proven twice: the write at 0x43C696 (lea eax,[esi+0x370]; mov byte ptr [eax],0; call 0x44B23D) and the read at 0x41874D (imul eax,eax,0x3D8; lea edx,[eax+ecx+0x370]; push edx), where the imul by the proven 0x3D8 record stride is what establishes the base register as a villager record. That it is a character array rather than a scalar is confirmed independently at 0x41C263 (mov byte ptr [esi+edx+0x370], bl), a single-byte store at a variable index into the buffer. LENGTH: bounded only by the displacement sweep of 0x340..0x3D8, which is dense -- every 4-byte slot in that range is referenced EXCEPT the run 0x374..0x388, and the next referenced slot is +0x38C (6 sites, a dword scalar). The sweep is positive-controlled: it finds +0x348 age, +0x350 gender, +0x360 head, +0x364 body, +0x36C id, +0x398 likes, +0x3A8 dislikes and +0x3BC skills, so the gap is a real absence and not a broken search. The buffer therefore spans 0x370..0x38B inclusive = 28 bytes. NOTE the copier enforces NOTHING: 0x44B23D is MSVC sprintf (unbounded -- it sets count 0x7FFFFFFF), not a length-limited copy, so the game itself provides no truncation guarantee and the 28-byte figure comes from the neighbouring-field bound alone. A consumer MUST treat the field as 28 bytes and force a NUL at byte 0x1B before use; assuming 24 would discard four name bytes and could make distinct villagers collide in an identity hash. Earlier displacement scans missed this buffer entirely because names are written by bulk string copies: the address is TAKEN (lea), never accessed as [reg+disp]. The prior entry's note that record[+0x374] lies INSIDE the name buffer was correct -- +0x374 is simply four bytes into it, which is why using it as mask storage silently renamed villagers.

name.evidence: Read site 0x41F39D: imul eax,eax,0xE48C; lea edx,[eax+ecx+0x564]; push edx; call 0x4682BD (sprintf) -- structurally identical to VV1's proven 0x41874D, and the imul by the 0xE48C stride is what establishes the base as a villager record. A villager-to-villager name copy at 0x421630/0x421638 has +0x564 on BOTH operands, both stride-indexed. LENGTH IS AN UPPER BOUND ONLY: VV2 writes via unbounded sprintf, so 0x19 comes from the displacement gap 0x564..0x57D, and the same gap method over-estimated VV1's buffer by 4 bytes. Never write more than 0x18.

absent_fields.nursing: REFUTED as nursing. record[+0x558] is a generic special/memorial flag used for exclusion, not nursing state; and VA 0x44B980 writes processed-age data at record[+0x540], which is likewise not a nursing flag. VV2 has no established nursing offset

absent_fields.elder_status: NOT ESTABLISHED as a meaning, though the storage IS established. record+0x7FC is genuinely a ONE-BYTE field on a villager record: every villager-side access is byte-sized (0x425051, 0x429C1D, 0x44C97F, 0x44CF74, 0x44D2BB, 0x44D4A2, 0x46513C), and the compiler emits mov dword for the skills at +0x7E4..+0x7F8 but mov byte for +0x7FC in the same straight-line block. The title selector at 0x429C15 (imul ecx,ecx,0xE48C; add ecx,edx; cmp byte ptr [ecx+0x7FC],bl; je; push 0x87) shows a non-zero byte makes the villager display as 'Esteemed Elder', bypassing the skill ladder; the same ecx feeds cmp dword ptr [ecx+0x530],0x118, which is how VV2's age offset was established. WHY THE MEANING IS STILL UNPROVEN: the only site that writes the literal 1 is 0x44D4A2, inside the reproduction routine 0x44D190, and it writes to the PARENT, not the newborn. Proven by the adjacent instructions: 0x44D48C copies [edi+0x530] into [esi+0x530], so edi is the source villager and esi the new one, and edi is loaded once at 0x44D257 and never reassigned. The read at 0x46513C is gated behind an age comparison. That is consistent with 'Esteemed Elder' but equally consistent with a has-bred latch that only matters once a villager is old. Do not treat it as a clean Elder boolean until the semantics are pinned down. TRAP RECORDED FOR FUTURE SCANS: a displacement-only search for +0x7FC also hits an AUDIO RESOURCE object at 0x43DC64, 0x43DFB4 and 0x43EFA3, where +0x7FC is a POINTER to a loaded sound. That class reuses +0x7E4..+0x7FC -- exactly the villager's skill range -- with +0x7E4 femsneeze.ogg, +0x7E8 giggles.ogg, +0x7EC gong2.ogg, +0x7F0 cooking.ogg, +0x7F4 chimestiny2.ogg, +0x7F8 chimeslow2.ogg, +0x7FC chimesmysterious.ogg. 0x43DFB4 is a one-line 'mov eax,[ecx+0x7FC]; ret 4' getter and 0x43EFA3 is its destructor release. Those dword accesses do NOT make the villager field a dword. Matching on displacement alone would conflate two unrelated classes.

vv4.title: Virtual Villagers - The Tree of Life

record.evidence: Accessor 0x466040: mov eax,[esp+4]; cmp eax,0x95; ja; imul eax,eax,0x2E3C; lea eax,[eax+ecx+0x44]; ret 4 -- structurally the twin of the proven grave accessor 0x45D650. ecx is the manager singleton 0x50E568, loaded as mov ecx,0x50E568 at all 55 call sites, so the array base is 0x50E568+0x44 = 0x50E5AC: 150 slots of 0x2E3C, spanning 0x50E5AC..0x6BFCD4, entirely inside .data. Cross-checked by the absolute references 0x510240/0x510244 (used at 0x43FFB3 and 0x442BB3 after imul eax,eax,0x2E3C), which resolve exactly to villager[N]+0x1C94/+0x1C98. The established name +0x1B9C and age +0x1B8C both fall inside the 0x2E3C record. NOTE: an earlier scan reported no stride multiply in 0x1000..0x4000; 0x2E3C is inside that range, so that scan was broken, not the game unindexed. capstone renders imul with THREE operands.

head.evidence: vv4_origins_icons.c VV_HEAD_OFFSET; inheritance writer sub_45EF10 confirmed to target this offset

name.evidence: vv4_origins_icons.c VV_NAME_OFFSET (24-byte villager name string, marked stable); independently re-confirmed by 0x45F3B3 (push 0x18; lea edx,[esi+0x1BC0]; call 0x4724E0 strncpy) -- a 24-byte copy, with the age threshold 0x168 tested on the same esi at 0x4481D0, which proves the base is a villager record. NOTE VV4 HAS TWO VILLAGER STRING BUFFERS and they are easy to confuse. +0x1BC0 is this one, the field the shipped mask feature reads. A SECOND buffer at +0x1B9C is the one used by the burial writer 0x45D4B4 (push 0x19; lea eax,[edi+0x1B9C]; call strncpy) and by the birth routine 0x460A1E, and it is the offset that matches VV5's +0x1B9C. Both are real. Do not 'correct' one to the other: an earlier attempt to do so would have changed what the shipped VV4 feature reads.

absent_fields.parentage: NOT STORED. No villager field holds another villager's pointer or index. Three independent lines: (1) a positive-controlled sweep of every villager-field load feeding a +0x1B9C/+0x1B90/+0x1B8C/+0x1B88 dereference finds only +0x834/+0x838 on a UI object and +0x1B88, the known self-pointer; (2) +0x1C04 and +0x1C08 -- which look like a parent pair because 0x45E81E zeroes them together -- are WRITE-ONLY: exactly one store each (0x45E83A, 0x45E856) and zero reads anywhere in the image, so they cannot function as a link; (3) the birth routine sub_460990 holds mother in ebp and father in esi and passes the other parent's NAME STRING BY VALUE (0x460A1E lea edx,[esi+0x1B9C]; push edx; mov ecx,ebp; call 0x45E7B0), so the child receives a copied string and genetics values, never a reference. sub_45E7B0's this IS a villager record (it calls the manager at 0x50E568 and every offset it touches, 0x1C04..0x1C60, is inside the 0x2E3C record); +0x1C10 receives a copy of the OTHER parent's name, which is what made it look like a second name field. The UI pointers at 0x416F60 +0x834/+0x838 are filled by virtual calls, not read off a villager. CONSEQUENCE: a parentage tracker cannot read a field off the child -- it must hook the moment of conception while both parent records are still live. Incidental correction: +0x1C94/+0x1C98 are screen X/Y coordinates computed at 0x43FF71 from floats plus the camera scroll globals 0x72563C/0x725640, not a parent pair.

identity_notes.stable_hash_inputs: Fields safe as identity-hash inputs are those written once and not rewritten in normal play. The name buffer qualifies in all five games. The preferred skill does NOT: it carries a -1 'none' sentinel and a player-driven toggler in VV3/VV4/VV5, so it changes at runtime by design. Head and body do not qualify either -- the VV3 appearance chooser rewrites them, which is why they were removed from the VV3 mask fingerprint after a mask was orphaned by a head-only edit.

conception_sites.purpose: Parentage cannot be read back off a child in any of the five games: inheritance computes the child's own appearance and keeps no parent pointer. It must instead be captured at conception, while both parent records are still live. These are the sites where that is possible. Every entry below was re-derived from the stock executables and spot-checked by disassembly rather than accepted as reported.

two_parent_call_sites.vv4: 0x004650EB (ecx = one parent, edi = the other) and 0x0046511B (ecx = edi). Gender at +0x1B90 decides which becomes the mother; esi is the acting villager and [esi+0x1B88] its self-pointer.
two_parent_call_sites.vv5: 0x0046E16B (ecx = [esi+0x1B88], edi = the partner) and 0x0046E19B (ecx = edi, other parent via eax). Structurally a clone of VV4: 0x46E138 mov ecx,[esi+0x1B88]; 0x46E13E cmp [ecx+0x1B90],1; jne. Stolen bytes e8907cffff and e8607cffff.
two_parent_call_sites.vv3: ONE call site only, 0x0045B8C9, because both branches converge on it. 0x45B89A tests gender at +0xDC8 directly with NO self-pointer indirection; the else branch at 0x45B8F8 sets up its arguments and jmps back. Both esi and edi are villager records there, but WHICH IS THE MOTHER IS PATH-DEPENDENT, so a hook must re-test [ecx+0xDC8] itself rather than assume.
two_parent_call_sites.vv2: 0x00464A38 in the dispatcher 0x00464680. edi is the acting villager; ebx is the partner BIASED BY +0x530, so the true record is ebx-0x530. That bias is inferred from field-offset arithmetic, not from watching the register be built, so verify in a debugger before shipping. A secondary two-record pair exists at 0x0044F8F0/0x0044F930 where ebx is UNBIASED.

hazards.vv3_jump_target: VERIFIED AND CRITICAL. 0x0045B8C9 is itself a jmp landing site, targeted by 0x45B91C (mov ecx,edi; jmp 0x45B8C9). Only the 5-byte call may be stolen. Extending the stolen bytes backwards puts a live landing site inside them and WILL crash the game.
hazards.vv2_ecx_is_not_the_mother: VERIFIED. VV2 is the outlier: 0x44B980 push edi; mov edi,ecx; ... then 0x44B990 mov eax,[esp+8]; imul eax,eax,0xE48C. So ecx is the MANAGER/array base and the mother is an INDEX in the first stack argument. VV3, VV4 and VV5 all pass the mother directly in ecx. A hook that assumes ecx is the mother will read the manager and log garbage. VV2's slot count is 0x100 (256), not the 150 the other games use.
hazards.relative_calls: Every one of these sites is a 5-byte relative E8. The rel32 must be recomputed if the instruction is relocated into a trampoline.
hazards.vv2_entry_stolen_bytes: The conception function's own entry bytes at 0x0044B980 contain a relative call at byte +3 (e8 88f9ffff), which likewise must be relocated if copied.

mate_finders.vv5: 0x00470A10, called at 0x0046E07E immediately before conception; matches VV4 predicate for predicate -- age >= 0x168 both sides, genders differ, not already pregnant, relatedness check, add esi,0x2F44 over 150 slots, returns -1 on failure

conception_sites.not_established: VV2's ebx bias and its +0x538 gender reading are inferred, not observed. Nothing here was confirmed against a live process; it is all static evidence. A debugger breakpoint at each site, checking that the named register points at a record whose name offset holds a readable name, would settle all of it.
